title: Shared helper contract for the .NET 10 port: queryHelpers, medicationScheduleUtils, notificationService, aiUsageLimiter, audit, cacheMiddleware (as consumed by visits.js / appointments.js / prescriptions.js)

findings.name: softDeleteFilter
findings.signature: const softDeleteFilter = { deletedAt: null }   // a plain object constant, NOT a function
findings.behaviour: It is a frozen-by-convention literal `{ deletedAt: null }` that routes spread into a Prisma `where`. Despite the docstring claiming it covers "Visit, Prescription, Appointment", the ONLY consumer in the entire repo is visits.js line 89: `let where = { ...softDeleteFilter };`. Verified by repo-wide grep: no other file imports it, and `deletedAt` appears nowhere in appointments.js or prescriptions.js. CONSEQUENCE THE PORT MUST PRESERVE: (a) GET /api/visits filters out soft-deleted visits; (b) GET /api/visits/:id does NOT (findUnique by id with no deletedAt guard, so a soft-deleted visit is still individually fetchable and returns 200); (c) GET /api/prescriptions and GET /api/appointments return soft-deleted rows — Prescription.deletedAt (schema line 694) and Appointment.deletedAt (schema line 1237) exist but are never filtered anywhere. Also note `deletedAt` is a scalar on Visit, so it IS emitted in the JSON body — the client receives `"deletedAt": null` on every row of the visits list (always null there, because of the filter), and a real ISO timestamp on prescriptions/appointments rows that happen to be soft-deleted. Models carrying deletedAt: Allergy(450), ChronicCondition(470), CurrentMedication(493), Visit(653), Prescription(694), Appointment(1237).
findings.portRecommendation: Do NOT implement this as an EF Core global query filter (`HasQueryFilter`) — that would silently start filtering prescriptions, appointments and GET /api/visits/:id, changing three response bodies. Model it as an opt-in extension method in a shared query module, e.g. `Tebrazi.Data.Querying.SoftDelete` → `public static IQueryable<T> NotSoftDeleted<T>(this IQueryable<T> q) where T : ISoftDeletable => q.Where(e => e.DeletedAt == null);` and call it at exactly one site: the visits list query. Keep `DeletedAt` in the serialized DTO for Visit/Prescription/Appointment as a nullable DateTime so `"deletedAt": null` still appears.

findings.name: parsePagination
findings.signature: parsePagination(query) => { page: number, limit: number, skip: number }
findings.behaviour: Body: `page = Math.max(1, parseInt(query.page) || 1)`; `limit = Math.min(Math.max(1, parseInt(query.limit) || 20), 100)`; `skip = (page - 1) * limit`. Defaults: page 1, limit 20. Cap: limit 100. Floor: limit 1, page 1. There is NO cap on page, so skip is unbounded. Only ONE call site in the whole repo: visits.js:87 (`const { page, limit, skip } = parsePagination(req.query);`). Prescriptions and appointments do not use it — prescriptions.js:168 hand-rolls `parseInt(req.query.limit) || 20` with NO cap for /interaction-history, and appointments.js:401 hard-codes `take: 200` with no pagination at all. JS parseInt quirks the port must reproduce exactly, because the client can send anything: `limit=0` → parseInt gives 0, which is falsy → falls to the `|| 20` default → limit 20 (NOT 1); but `limit=-5` → -5 is truthy → Math.max(1,-5)=1 → limit 1. That asymmetry is real. `limit=1e3` → parseInt stops at 'e' → 1. `limit=0x10` → parseInt auto-detects hex → 16. `limit=12abc` → 12 (lenient prefix parse; int.TryParse would reject it). `limit=3.9` → 3. `limit=%20 7 %20` → 7 (leading whitespace tolerated). Repeated params `?page=1&page=2` → Express yields the array ['1','2'] → parseInt coerces to "1,2" → 1. Non-numeric → NaN → default. HOW THE ROUTE USES THE RESULT: `take: limit, skip` on `prisma.visit.findMany`, and a parallel `prisma.visit.count({ where })`. ENVELOPE: visits.js builds it by hand — `const pagination = { total, page, limit, pages: Math.ceil(total / limit) };` then `res.json({ data: <rows>, pagination })`. Exactly four pagination keys, in that order: total, page, limit, pages. There is NO `success` flag, NO `hasMore`, NO `timestamp`. total=0 → pages 0. Early exit when the physician has no PhysicianProfile: `res.json({ data: [], pagination: { total: 0, page, limit, pages: 0 } })` — note page/limit are the parsed values, not hard-coded, and `pages` is literally 0 (not Math.ceil). `data` is always an array, never null; empty array when there are no rows.
findings.portRecommendation: Own it in `Tebrazi.Web.Querying.PaginationParser` as `public static PageRequest Parse(IQueryCollection q)` returning `readonly record struct PageRequest(int Page, int Limit, int Skip)`. Implement a `JsParseInt(StringValues) → int?` helper that mimics JS: take the first value if repeated (after joining with ','), trim leading whitespace, honour a leading 0x/0X as hex, accept a leading sign, consume the longest valid integer prefix and stop at the first invalid char, return null on no digits. Then apply the falsy-zero rule verbatim: `var p = JsParseInt(q["page"]); page = Math.Max(1, (p is null or 0) ? 1 : p.Value); var l = JsParseInt(q["limit"]); limit = Math.Min(Math.Max(1, (l is null or 0) ? 20 : l.Value), 100);`. For the envelope, define `sealed record PagedEnvelope<T>(IReadOnlyList<T> Data, PageMeta Pagination)` and `sealed record PageMeta(int Total, int Page, int Limit, int Pages)` with System.Text.Json camelCase and property order total/page/limit/pages. Put the envelope in a Visits-specific contracts namespace, not a shared one — nothing else on the client contract uses this shape.

findings.name: lib/response.js success/error/paginated (dead code — do NOT port as the shared envelope)
findings.signature: success(res, data, message='Success', statusCode=200); error(res, message='Internal server error', statusCode=500, details=null); paginated(res, data, total, { page, limit })
findings.behaviour: This module defines a `{ success: true, data, message }` / `{ success: false, error[, details] }` / `{ success, data, pagination: { total, page, limit, pages, hasMore } }` envelope — and NONE of visits.js, appointments.js, prescriptions.js import it (verified: `grep -n 'lib/response' ` over all three returns nothing). A third, different envelope exists at server/src/sdk/responses/pagination.js (`{ success, data, pagination: { page, limit, total, totalPages, hasNext, hasPrev }, timestamp }`), also unused by these routes. So three competing pagination shapes live in the repo and only the hand-rolled visits.js one is on the client contract. Error bodies in the three route files are likewise hand-rolled bare objects, not the helper's: e.g. `{ error: 'Failed to list visits', detail: error.message }` (note the key is `detail`, singular, on visits list only), `{ error: 'Visit not found' }`, `{ error: 'Access denied' }`, `{ error: 'Failed to get visit', details: <message or undefined> }` (that one is `details`, plural, and the key is OMITTED entirely when NODE_ENV !== 'development' because `undefined` is dropped by JSON.stringify).
findings.portRecommendation: Do not introduce an ApiResponse<T> wrapper or a ProblemDetails-based error filter for these three controllers — either would break every client call site. Return bare anonymous/record DTOs. Add a `JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull`-equivalent only where the Node code relies on `undefined` being dropped (the `details` key on GET /api/visits/:id 500, and `patientName` on the prescriptions list — see the prescriptions finding). Everywhere else nulls are explicitly serialized, so a blanket WhenWritingNull is wrong; prefer per-property `[JsonIgnore(Condition = WhenWritingNull)]`.

findings.name: parseFrequency
findings.signature: parseFrequency(frequency: string) => { dosesPerDay: number, intervalHours: number }
findings.behaviour:
Normalises with `frequency.toLowerCase().trim()` — THROWS TypeError if frequency is null/undefined/a number (see the throw-path finding). Then an if/else-if CHAIN, first match wins, evaluated in this exact order:
1. /every\s*(\d+)\s*h/i → dosesPerDay = Math.round(24 / hours). Matches "every 8 hours", "every8h", "every 6 hrs", "q every 12 h". Quirks: "every 5 hours" → round(4.8) = 5. "every 36 hours" → round(0.667) = 1 (q36h silently becomes once daily). "every 0 hours" → 24/0 = Infinity → Math.round(Infinity) = Infinity → clamped to 12 (no crash, no NaN).
2. /(\d+)\s*times?\s*(a\s*day|daily|\/\s*day)/i → re-extracts the digit with a SECOND, looser regex /(\d+)\s*times?/i. Matches "3 times a day", "3 time daily", "3 times/day", "3times a day", "1 time a day". DOES NOT match "3 times per day" (no "per" alternative) — that string falls through the whole chain and yields dosesPerDay 1. Same for "3 x daily"? no — "3 x daily" has no "times", so it falls to branch 4 via /2\s*x/? no, only literal 2 — so it ends at 1 unless the digit is 1/2/4.
3. /three\s*times|thrice|t\.?i\.?d/i → 3
4. /twice|two\s*times|b\.?i\.?d|2\s*x/i → 2
5. /four\s*times|q\.?i\.?d|4\s*x/i → 4
6. /once|one\s*time|o\.?d|1\s*x/i → 1
No match → dosesPerDay stays at its initialised value 1. There is no error, no sentinel, no null: unknown input is silently once-daily.
UNANCHORED-SUBSTRING QUIRKS (these are real and must be reproduced): none of the abbreviation alternatives are word-bounded, and the dots are optional, so `t?i?d` matches inside "antidote" → 3; `b?i?d` matches inside "morbid"/"forbidden" → 2; `o?d` matches inside "food", "period", "odd", "sodium", "as needed"? ("needed" has no 'od'; "as directed" has no 'od') → but "one tablet with food" → matches `o.?d` in "food" → 1 (which happens to be right by luck), and "take with sodium bicarb" → 1. Ordering also matters: TID is tested BEFORE BID and QID, so a string containing both patterns resolves to 3.
CLAMP AND RETURN: `dosesPerDay = Math.max(1, Math.min(dosesPerDay, 12))` then `intervalHours = Math.round(24 / dosesPerDay)`. So "99 times a day" → 12; "0 times a day" → parseInt("0")=0 → clamped to 1. intervalHours is a ROUNDED integer and is deliberately inconsistent with getDefaultDoseTimes' exact spacing: 5 doses → intervalHours 5 (but dose times are spaced 4.8h); 7 → 3 (actual 3.43h); 9 → 3 (actual 2.67h); 11 → 2 (actual 2.18h). Both values are persisted — intervalHours goes into the Reminder.notes JSON while the actual dose times come from getDefaultDoseTimes.
CONSUMERS: prescriptions.js:365 (PUT /api/prescriptions/:id/send, inside the auto-reminder loop) and reminders.js:234 (POST /api/reminders/medication-schedule). reminders.js uses only intervalHours (spacing doses from a caller-supplied firstDoseTime) and never calls getDefaultDoseTimes; prescriptions.js uses only dosesPerDay for the times and stores intervalHours in notes.
findings.portRecommendation: Own it in `Tebrazi.Domain.Medications.MedicationSchedule` as `public static (int DosesPerDay, int IntervalHours) ParseFrequency(string frequency)`. Use `System.Text.RegularExpressions` with `RegexOptions.IgnoreCase` and the SAME unanchored patterns — do NOT 'fix' them by adding \b word boundaries, and do NOT reorder the chain. Compile them as static readonly Regex (or [GeneratedRegex]). Reproduce `Math.Round(24.0/hours)` with `MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero` (JS Math.round rounds .5 toward +Infinity; C# Math.Round defaults to banker's rounding, which would turn round(24/48)=round(0.5) from 1 into 0). Handle hours==0 as `double.PositiveInfinity` → clamp to 12 rather than dividing by zero on ints. Signature should take `string?` and throw the same way (or the caller must guard) — see the throw-path finding before choosing.

findings.name: getDefaultDoseTimes
findings.signature: getDefaultDoseTimes(dosesPerDay: number) => string[]   // "HH:mm" strings, 24-hour, zero-padded
findings.behaviour:
A switch with four hard-coded medically-sensible tables and a computed default:
  1 → ['08:00']
  2 → ['08:00','20:00']
  3 → ['08:00','14:00','20:00']   (NOT evenly spaced — 6h/6h/12h)
  4 → ['08:00','12:00','18:00','22:00']   (NOT evenly spaced — 4h/6h/4h/10h)
  default (0, 5+, negatives, non-integers) → evenly spaced from 08:00: `intervalHours = 24 / dosesPerDay`; for i in 0..dosesPerDay-1: `totalMinutes = (8*60 + i*intervalHours*60) % (24*60)`; `h = Math.floor(totalMinutes/60)`; `m = Math.round(totalMinutes % 60)`; push `${pad2(h)}:${pad2(m)}`.
Because `%` is applied to the running total, the list WRAPS PAST MIDNIGHT and is therefore not sorted: 5 → ['08:00','12:48','17:36','22:24','03:12']; 6 → ['08:00','12:00','16:00','20:00','00:00','04:00']; 7 → ['08:00','11:26','14:51','18:17','21:43','01:09','04:34']; 12 → 08:00,10:00,…,04:00,06:00. Fractional minutes are rounded per-element, so the times drift and are not exactly interval-spaced. dosesPerDay=0 → interval = Infinity → 0 iterations → returns [] (an EMPTY array, not null) — reachable only if called directly, since parseFrequency clamps to 1..12. Negative input → 0 iterations → []. `m = Math.round(totalMinutes % 60)` can in principle produce 60 and emit an invalid "HH:60"; I checked every value 5..12 and none does (the worst case is d=11, m→55), so within the clamped range it is safe, but a direct call with d≥13 can break it.
ONLY CONSUMER: prescriptions.js:366. reminders.js does not import it. In prescriptions.js each returned "HH:mm" is split on ':' and mapped to a LOCAL-TIME Date for today via `doseTime.setHours(h, m, 0, 0)`; if that instant is already in the past (`doseTime < new Date()`), the date is bumped one day (`setDate(getDate()+1)`). So a 5-dose schedule whose '03:12' entry has passed starts tomorrow while '08:00' may start today — the reminders in one prescription can straddle two dates. The dose label is `''` when dosesPerDay===1 and ` (Dose i+1/N)` otherwise, and the human time in the description uses `toLocaleTimeString('en-US', { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit', hour12: true })` → e.g. "08:00 AM", "01:09 AM" (note 2-digit hour, so a leading zero, and a non-breaking-space vs regular space depends on ICU version).
findings.portRecommendation: Same owner as parseFrequency: `Tebrazi.Domain.Medications.MedicationSchedule.GetDefaultDoseTimes(int dosesPerDay) → IReadOnlyList<string>`. Keep the four literal tables verbatim (they are clinical defaults, not a formula — a naive even-spacing implementation would change 3-dose and 4-dose schedules). In the computed branch use `double` arithmetic and `Math.Round(x, MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero)`, keep the `% 1440` on the running total so the wrap-past-midnight ordering is preserved, and return an empty list (not null, not a throw) for 0/negative. Format with `h.ToString("D2") + ":" + m.ToString("D2")` — never a culture-sensitive TimeSpan/DateTime format. On the caller side, the 'HH:mm' → today/tomorrow projection and the `toLocaleTimeString('en-US')` label must be reproduced with an explicit `CultureInfo("en-US")` and the `hh:mm tt` pattern, and the same server-local-time semantics (see the timezone note in getMonthlyUsage).

findings.name: createNotification
findings.signature: async createNotification({ userId, type, title, message, data = null, sendEmail = false, sendPush = false }) => Notification
findings.behaviour:
Single destructured options object; five of the seven keys have defaults (`data = null`, `sendEmail = false`, `sendPush = false`); userId/type/title/message have none, so omitting them writes `undefined` → Prisma rejects the row for the three non-nullable String columns. ROW WRITTEN (server/prisma/schema.prisma:1648, table `notifications`): only FOUR columns are supplied — `{ userId, type, title, message, data }`. Everything else comes from DB/Prisma defaults: `id` = `@default(uuid())` → a v4 UUID (NOT a cuid — ActivityLog and AiAuditLog use cuid, Notification uses uuid; the id format is visible to the client), `isRead` = `false`, `readAt` = NULL, `createdAt` = `@default(now())`. `data` is `Json?` and is passed straight through — every call site in the three route files passes a small flat object (see below), so it lands as a JSON object; a caller who passes nothing gets literal NULL, not `{}`. NO VALIDATION AT ALL: `type` is not checked against the exported NOTIFICATION_TYPES array (separate finding), userId is not checked for existence, and the Notification model has NO relation/FK to User (grep of schema.prisma shows no `user User @relation` on Notification and no `notifications` back-reference on User) — so a notification for a deleted or bogus userId inserts cleanly. FAILURE SEMANTICS — the important part: the `prisma.notification.create` is NOT wrapped in try/catch, so a DB failure THROWS out of createNotification. Every one of the 18 call sites in the three route files wraps the call in its own try/catch that only logs (`catch (e) { logger.error(...) }`), so in practice the request still succeeds and the client never learns the notification was lost. The two dispatch blocks that follow, by contrast, SWALLOW everything: (a) the email block runs only `if (sendEmail)`, looks up `{ email, displayName }` for the user, and if `user?.email` is truthy calls emailService.sendEmail with `subject: title`, `html: '

{title}

{message}

'` (raw interpolation — no escaping, an XSS/HTML-injection vector if title/message contain markup), `text: '{title}\n\n{message}'`; any throw is caught and console.error'd; (b) the push block is OUTSIDE any flag check — `sendPush` is destructured but NEVER READ anywhere in the function body, so `pushService.send(userId, { title, body: message, data: data || {} })` is attempted on EVERY createNotification call, including visits.js:1320-1321 which explicitly passes `sendEmail: false, sendPush: false`. Its catch is deliberately quiet: it re-logs only if `err.message` exists and does not contain the substring 'findMany'. pushService.send itself short-circuits to `{ sent: 0, method: 'in-app-only' }` when the user has no DeviceToken rows, so with no FCM config the push path is a wasted DeviceToken query per notification. Note the `data` shape differs between the row and the push payload: the row stores `data` (possibly null), the push gets `data || {}` with every value String()-ified. RETURN VALUE: the created Notification row. None of the 18 call sites in visits.js/appointments.js/prescriptions.js use the return value except visits.js indirectly — so it is effectively fire-and-log. AWAIT ORDERING: the function awaits the email dispatch and then the push dispatch before returning, so a slow SMTP/FCM call adds latency to the HTTP request that triggered it. appointments.js POST / awaits it inline before `res.status(201).json(appointment)`. CALL SITES AND EXACT ARGS in the three files (userId / type / data / flags): visits.js:438 patient/FOLLOW_UP_SET/{visitId,followUpDate}/sendEmail true; visits.js:532 patient/VISIT_COMPLETED/{visitId}/sendEmail true; visits.js:557 staff.userId/VISIT_COMPLETED_STAFF/{visitId,patientUserId,...}/no flags; visits.js:648 physician/PATIENT_FEEDBACK/{visitId}/sendEmail false; visits.js:1314 patient/FOLLOW_UP_REMINDER/{visitId}/sendEmail false,sendPush false (unreachable — see the dead-route finding). appointments.js:490 physician/NEW_APPOINTMENT_REQUEST/{appointmentId,patientUserId}/sendEmail true; :614 physician/PATIENT_ARRIVED/{appointmentId,patientUserId,clinicId}/no flags; :768 patient/APPOINTMENT_CONFIRMED/{appointmentId}/sendEmail true; :827 physician/APPOINTMENT_CANCELLED/{appointmentId}/no flags; :837 patient/APPOINTMENT_CANCELLED/{appointmentId}/sendEmail true; :1019 physician/PATIENT_ARRIVED/{appointmentId,patientUserId,room}/no flags; :1188 physician/INTAKE_NOTE_READY/{appointmentId,noteId,patientUserId}/no flags. prescriptions.js:339 patient/PRESCRIPTION_SENT/{prescriptionId}/sendEmail true; :415 patient/MEDICATION_REMINDER_SET/{prescriptionId}/sendEmail false; :562 physician/REFILL_REQUEST/{prescriptionId}/sendEmail false; :620 patient/REFILL_RESPONSE/{prescriptionId}/sendEmail true.
findings.portRecommendation: Own it in `Tebrazi.Application.Notifications.INotificationService` with `Task<Notification> CreateAsync(CreateNotificationRequest req, CancellationToken ct)` and `sealed record CreateNotificationRequest(string UserId, string Type, string Title, string Message, JsonDocument? Data = null, bool SendEmail = false, bool SendPush = false)`. Reproduce exactly: insert only the five columns and let the DB supply Id/IsRead/CreatedAt; generate Id as `Guid.NewGuid().ToString()` (lowercase, hyphenated, v4) NOT a sequential/NEWSEQUENTIALID default, because the client sees it; let the insert THROW (do not add a catch inside the service — the callers' swallow-and-log is the contract); always attempt push regardless of SendPush and swallow its failure; keep SendPush in the DTO as an accepted-but-ignored parameter (or delete it and fix the two call sites, but that changes push volume). Do NOT add an FK from Notification.UserId to Users in the SQL Server schema — an FK would start rejecting rows that Postgres accepts today. Escape nothing in the email HTML if you want byte-identical mail, but flag the injection to the owner. Consider making email/push dispatch fire-and-forget via a background queue only if you are willing to change request latency; the Node version awaits them.

findings.name: NOTIFICATION_TYPES is exported but never enforced — 7 live types are missing from it
findings.signature: const NOTIFICATION_TYPES = [ 19 strings ]   // exported; zero references from createNotification
findings.behaviour: The array lists 19 types (CONNECTION_REQUEST, CONNECTION_ACCEPTED, LAB_RESULT_UPLOADED, DRUG_INTERACTION_ALERT, FAMILY_HEALTH_ALERT, APPOINTMENT_BOOKED, APPOINTMENT_CONFIRMED, APPOINTMENT_CANCELLED, APPOINTMENT_REMINDER, VISIT_COMPLETED, PRESCRIPTION_SENT, FOLLOW_UP_REMINDER, MESSAGE_RECEIVED, NEWSFEED_MENTION, PATIENT_ARRIVED, INTAKE_NOTE_READY, STAFF_INVITED, STAFF_JOINED, SYSTEM) and Notification.type is a plain `String` in the schema, not an enum. createNotification never consults the array. Seven types actually written by the three route files are NOT in it: FOLLOW_UP_SET, VISIT_COMPLETED_STAFF, PATIENT_FEEDBACK (visits.js), NEW_APPOINTMENT_REQUEST (appointments.js — note the list contains APPOINTMENT_BOOKED, which is never used), MEDICATION_REMINDER_SET, REFILL_REQUEST, REFILL_RESPONSE (prescriptions.js). So the notifications table legitimately contains type values outside the documented set, and the client must be assumed to switch on the raw string.
findings.portRecommendation: Model `Notification.Type` as `string` (nvarchar) with NO CHECK constraint and NO C# enum, and expose the 19-item list only as a `public static class NotificationTypes` of const strings for authoring convenience. If the port introduces an enum + `JsonStringEnumConverter`, the seven unlisted types become either a deserialization failure or a numeric value in the JSON — both break the client. Owner: `Tebrazi.Domain.Notifications`.

findings.name: aiUsageCheck middleware
findings.signature: aiUsageCheck(agentName: string) => async (req, res, next) => void   // Express middleware factory
findings.behaviour:
Applied in the three files at: visits.js:674 POST /:id/generate-soap → 'soap'; visits.js:964 POST /:id/transcribe → 'scribe' (registered AFTER `upload.single('audio')`, so multer parses and buffers the whole audio file BEFORE the quota check runs — a limit-blocked request still pays the upload); visits.js:1023 POST /:id/suggest-codes → 'icd10'; prescriptions.js:972 POST /transcribe-rx → 'scribe' (same post-multer ordering). appointments.js does NOT use it (its /ai-optimize route at line 1328 calls aiGateway with no quota check at all).
STEPS AND EXIT POINTS, in order:
1. `req.user?.id` missing → `401 { "error": "Authentication required" }`. (Unreachable in these files: `router.use(authCheck)` already 401s with `{"error":"No token provided"}` / `{"error":"Invalid token"}`.)
2. `prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id }, select: { id, userType, subscriptionTier } })`. Not found → `401 { "error": "User not found" }` (401, not 404).
3. Tier resolution via getUserTier (separate finding).
4. Unknown tier name (no TIER_LIMITS entry) → console.warn and `next()` — NO limit enforced and `req.aiUsage` left UNDEFINED.
5. Agent gate: `if (tier.allowedAgents.length > 0 && !tier.allowedAgents.includes(agentName))` → `403` with body exactly `{ "error": "Feature not available on your plan", "message": "The <Pretty Name> feature requires a Pro subscription.", "upgradeRequired": true, "currentTier": "<TIER>" }`. The pretty name comes from formatAgentName's map (soap→'AI SOAP Generator', icd10→'ICD-10 Auto-Coder', drug_check→'Drug Interaction Checker', scribe→'Medical Scribe', health_chat→'Health Assistant', smart_reply→'Smart Reply', cds→'Clinical Decision Support', scheduler→'Smart Scheduler', clinical_reference→'Clinical Reference', clinic_ai→'Clinic Intelligence'), falling back to the raw agent key. Note the message hard-codes "requires a Pro subscription" even when the caller is already PRO. Relevant to these files: a PATIENT_FREE/PATIENT_FAMILY user (allowedAgents = ['health_chat'] only) hitting generate-soap / transcribe / suggest-codes / transcribe-rx gets this 403.
6. Quota gate, skipped entirely when `tier.monthlyAiCalls === Infinity` (CLINIC). Otherwise getMonthlyUsage runs and if `usage.callCount >= tier.monthlyAiCalls` → `429` with body exactly `{ "error": "Monthly AI limit reached", "message": "You've used <n>/<limit> AI calls this month. Upgrade to Pro for more.", "upgradeRequired": true, "currentTier": "<TIER>", "usage": { "used": <n>, "limit": <limit>, "totalTokens": <int>, "totalCost": <float>, "resetsAt": "<ISO8601 with ms, Z>" } }`. The apostrophe in "You've" is a plain ASCII '. `resetsAt` is `getNextMonthStart().toISOString()` = first day of next month at 00:00 SERVER-LOCAL time, then converted to UTC — so on a UTC+2 host it serializes as e.g. "2026-09-30T22:00:00.000Z", not "2026-10-01T00:00:00.000Z". totalCost is an unrounded float here (contrast getMyUsage, which does toFixed(4)); it is 0 when the _sum is null.
7. On success it attaches `req.aiUsage = { used, limit, remaining, tier }` (metered tiers) or `{ used: 0, limit: Infinity, remaining: Infinity, tier }` (CLINIC), then `next()`.
8. CATCH-ALL: any throw (DB down, etc.) is console.error'd and the request is allowed through — explicitly fail-open "for clinical safety" — leaving `req.aiUsage` undefined.
The quota is a SINGLE GLOBAL per-user monthly counter: getMonthlyUsage does not filter by agent, so a physician's 500 PRO calls are shared across soap+icd10+scribe+everything. The counter never resets mid-month and there is no per-call increment here — the count comes from AiAuditLog rows written later by aiGateway.logAudit (server/src/services/aiGateway.js:112), so a request that passes the gate and then fails inside the gateway may or may not consume quota depending on the `success` flag written.
TIER TABLE (TIER_LIMITS): FREE {50 calls, agents [soap,icd10,scribe,cds,drug_check,clinic_ai,clinical_reference], maxTokensPerCall 1500}; PRO {500, [soap,icd10,drug_check,scribe,health_chat,smart_reply,cds,scheduler,clinical_reference,clinic_ai], 3000}; CLINIC {Infinity, same 10 agents, 4000}; PATIENT_FREE {20, [health_chat], 1000}; PATIENT_FAMILY {100, [health_chat], 2000}. `maxTokensPerCall` is defined but NEVER read by the middleware or by anything in the three route files — dead config.
findings.portRecommendation: Own it as an ASP.NET Core `IAsyncActionFilter` (not middleware — it needs the action's agent name), e.g. `[AiUsage("soap")]` → `Tebrazi.Web.Filters.AiUsageAttribute` + `Tebrazi.Application.Ai.IAiUsageLimiter`. Register the filter AFTER model binding so the multipart body is already read, matching the post-multer ordering on the two transcribe routes. Return the error bodies as literal anonymous objects / dedicated records so key order and wording match byte-for-byte (including "You've" with an ASCII apostrophe and the hard-coded "requires a Pro subscription"). Represent Infinity as `int?` = null internally with an explicit `IsUnlimited` flag rather than `double.PositiveInfinity`, but see the Infinity-serialization finding for what must appear in JSON. Keep the fail-open catch-all: wrap the whole filter body in try/catch and call `await next()` on any exception, logging only. Store the tier table as a static readonly dictionary in `Tebrazi.Application.Ai.TierLimits`; keep MaxTokensPerCall present but unused so a later port stage can wire it.

findings.name: getUserTier — tier resolution quirks the port must copy
findings.signature: getUserTier(user: { userType, subscriptionTier }) => string
findings.behaviour: `if (user.userType === 'PATIENT') { return user.subscriptionTier === 'PATIENT_FAMILY' ? 'PATIENT_FAMILY' : 'PATIENT_FREE'; }` then `if (user.subscriptionTier) return user.subscriptionTier;` else `'FREE'`. Consequences: (a) a PATIENT whose subscriptionTier is 'PRO' or 'CLINIC' is FORCED down to PATIENT_FREE (20 calls, health_chat only) — patients can never buy physician tiers; (b) for every non-PATIENT userType the RAW subscriptionTier string is returned unvalidated, so a physician row carrying 'PATIENT_FAMILY' gets patient limits (100 calls, health_chat only → 403 on soap), and a row carrying anything unrecognised ('ENTERPRISE', 'TRIAL', a typo) produces `TIER_LIMITS[x] === undefined` → the unknown-tier branch → completely UNLIMITED, unmetered access with `req.aiUsage` undefined. subscriptionTier is `String @default("FREE")` and non-nullable (schema.prisma:112), so the `|| 'FREE'` fallback only fires on an empty string. IMPORTANT DIVERGENCE: aiUsageCheck reads userType/subscriptionTier FRESH FROM THE DB, whereas the route handlers in visits.js/appointments.js/prescriptions.js read `req.user.userType` from the JWT payload (auth.js sets `req.user = jwt.verify(...)`; the token carries id, email, role, userType, displayName and lasts 7d). So after a userType or tier change the quota gate sees the new value immediately while the route's physician/patient branching still sees the stale token value until re-login.
findings.portRecommendation: Put it next to the tier table in `Tebrazi.Application.Ai.TierResolver.Resolve(string userType, string subscriptionTier) → string`. Return a plain string, not an enum, and look it up in a `Dictionary<string, TierLimits>` with a null-miss → unlimited-and-unmetered branch. Keep the fresh DB read inside the filter and keep the route handlers reading userType from the ClaimsPrincipal (`User.FindFirst("userType")`), preserving the stale-token divergence — unifying them would change who sees which branch of the list endpoints.

findings.name: getMonthlyUsage — the counting query, and its timezone-sensitive month boundary
findings.signature: async getMonthlyUsage(userId) => { callCount: number, totalTokens: number, totalCost: number }
findings.behaviour: `monthStart = new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), 1)` — midnight on the 1st in the SERVER'S LOCAL timezone, not UTC. Then a single Prisma aggregate over AiAuditLog with `where: { userId, createdAt: { gte: monthStart }, success: true, cached: false }`, `_count: { id: true }`, `_sum: { tokensUsed: true, costUsd: true }`. Returns `{ callCount: result._count.id || 0, totalTokens: result._sum.tokensUsed || 0, totalCost: result._sum.costUsd || 0 }` — the `|| 0` matters because Prisma returns null for _sum over an empty set. NOT filtered by agent (global per-user quota) and NOT filtered by clinic/organization. Excluded from the count: failed calls (`success: false`) and cache hits (`cached: false` — "cached calls are free"). AiAuditLog rows are written only by aiGateway.logAudit (server/src/services/aiGateway.js:110-118), which itself swallows insert failures — so a DB hiccup silently grants free quota. AiAuditLog.tokensUsed is `Int?` and costUsd is `Float?`, so both sums can be null even with rows present. AiAuditLog DOES have an FK to User (schema.prisma:1879), unlike Notification and ActivityLog. `getNextMonthStart()` = `new Date(y, m + 1, 1)` — also local, and JS handles the December rollover automatically. Both the 429 body's `resetsAt` and getMyUsage's `resetsAt`/`billingPeriod` are these local dates rendered through toISOString(), i.e. shifted into UTC.
findings.portRecommendation: `Tebrazi.Application.Ai.AiUsageRepository.GetMonthlyUsageAsync(string userId, CancellationToken ct)` returning `readonly record struct AiUsage(int CallCount, int TotalTokens, double TotalCost)`. Compute the boundary as `var now = DateTime.Now; var monthStart = new DateTime(now.Year, now.Month, 1, 0, 0, 0, DateTimeKind.Local);` — deliberately DateTime.Now/Local, not UtcNow — then convert to UTC for the comparison if CreatedAt is stored as UTC, so the window matches Node on the same host TZ. Use `.SumAsync(x => (int?)x.TokensUsed) ?? 0` and `?? 0.0` to reproduce the null→0 coalesce. Serialize resetsAt with `ToUniversalTime().ToString("yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffZ")` to match JS toISOString()'s exact 3-digit-ms + Z format. Flag the local-timezone month boundary to the owner as a deliberate carry-over, since a container TZ change silently shifts everyone's billing window.

findings.name: Infinity → null: the aiUsage echo in the generate-soap response body
findings.signature: visits.js:905 — `aiUsage: req.aiUsage || null` inside the POST /api/visits/:id/generate-soap success body
findings.behaviour: This is the ONLY place in the three route files where req.aiUsage reaches the client (grep confirms: no aiUsage reference in appointments.js or prescriptions.js). Three distinct JSON outcomes: (1) metered tier → `"aiUsage": { "used": 12, "limit": 500, "remaining": 488, "tier": "PRO" }`; (2) CLINIC tier → req.aiUsage is `{ used: 0, limit: Infinity, remaining: Infinity, tier: 'CLINIC' }`, and JSON.stringify renders Infinity as **null**, so the wire body is `"aiUsage": { "used": 0, "limit": null, "remaining": null, "tier": "CLINIC" }` — not 0, not a big number, not the string "unlimited"; (3) unknown tier or the fail-open catch → req.aiUsage undefined → `"aiUsage": null`. Note that unrelated helper getMyUsage (GET /api/ai-usage/my-usage, not one of these three files) takes the opposite approach for the same concept, emitting the literal STRING "unlimited" for monthlyAiCalls/callsRemaining — so the two endpoints disagree and the port must not normalise them. The full generate-soap body key order is: message, subjective, objective, assessment, plan, aiProvider, aiModel, enhanced, aiUsage, specialtyData, specialtyKey.
findings.portRecommendation: Model the echoed object as `sealed record AiUsageEcho(int Used, int? Limit, int? Remaining, string Tier)` and pass null for Limit/Remaining on unlimited tiers, with the whole property nullable so the undefined case yields `"aiUsage": null`. Do NOT use `double` with PositiveInfinity — System.Text.Json throws on non-finite doubles by default and, with `JsonNumberHandling.AllowNamedFloatingPointLiterals`, would emit "Infinity" as a string. Do not add `WhenWritingNull` to these properties: the keys must still be present with null values. Owner: the Visits controller's response contracts, with the record itself in `Tebrazi.Application.Ai`.

findings.name: auditLog (res.json-intercepting middleware)
findings.signature: auditLog(action: string, resource: string) => (req, res, next) => void
findings.behaviour:
Only TWO call sites across the three files, both on create: visits.js:182 `router.post('/', auditLog('CREATE','visit'), handler)` and prescriptions.js:99 `router.post('/', auditLog('CREATE','prescription'), handler)`. appointments.js writes NO audit rows at all — booking, confirm, cancel, complete, no-show, check-in and DELETE /:id are all unaudited.
MECHANISM: it monkey-patches `res.json` before the handler runs. Inside the patched function it checks `res.statusCode < 400 && req.user?.id` and, if both hold, fires `prisma.activityLog.create(...)` WITHOUT awaiting, with `.catch(() => {})` — fully fire-and-forget: it never blocks the response, never fails the request, and an insert error is silently discarded (no log line at all). It then calls the original res.json. Because the check happens inside the patched call, `res.status(201)` has already been applied, so a 201 IS audited. Error paths (`res.status(400|403|404|500).json(...)`) are >= 400 and are NOT audited. Anything that responds via res.send/res.end/res.sendStatus/streaming bypasses the patch entirely (relevant to prescriptions.js GET /:id/pdf, which is not audited anyway). If a handler calls res.json twice, two rows are written.
ROW WRITTEN into `activity_logs` (schema.prisma:1887): `userId` = req.user.id (from the JWT, not the DB); `action` = the literal first arg ('CREATE'); `resource` = the literal second arg ('visit' / 'prescription'); `resourceId` = `req.params?.id || data?.id || null`, then `String()`-ified if truthy — req.params.id WINS over the body, and since these are both POST / routes with no :id it always falls through to `data.id`, which works because both handlers return the created entity directly (`res.status(201).json(visit)` at visits.js:257, `res.status(201).json(prescription)` at prescriptions.js:127). Had either handler wrapped its payload in an envelope, resourceId would silently become null; `metadata` = `{ method: req.method, path: req.originalUrl, ...(req.body?.reason ? { reason: req.body.reason } : {}) }` — `path` is the FULL original URL including the /api mount and any query string, and the conditional `reason` spread is dead for both of these routes (visits POST body is {clinicId, patientUserId, subprofileId, clinicPatientId, chiefComplaint, rawNotes, appointmentId}; prescriptions POST body is {visitId, medications, notes} — neither has `reason`); `ipAddress` = `req.ip || req.connection?.remoteAddress || null` — there is NO `app.set('trust proxy')` anywhere in server/src/index.js, so behind a load balancer this records the proxy's address, not the client's; `userAgent` = `req.get('User-Agent')?.slice(0, 256) || null` — truncated to 256 chars, and an absent header yields null. DB-supplied: `id` = `@default(cuid())` (a cuid, NOT a uuid — Notification uses uuid; if any client ever surfaces these ids the format differs) and `createdAt` = now(). ActivityLog has NO FK to User (no relation on either side in the schema), so orphan rows insert fine.
Nothing in these three route files ever READS activity_logs; the reader is routes/analytics.js (/recent-activity, cacheMiddleware(30)).
findings.portRecommendation: Own it as `Tebrazi.Web.Filters.AuditLogAttribute : Attribute, IAsyncActionFilter` in an Audit module, applied as `[AuditLog("CREATE", "visit")]`. Do NOT implement it as an EF SaveChanges interceptor or ASP.NET middleware — the Node version keys off the response status and the response body's `id`, so the filter must inspect the executed result: after `await next()`, if the `ObjectResult`'s StatusCode (defaulting to 200 when null) is < 400 and the user is authenticated, read the id via `RouteData.Values["id"] ?? <reflected/serialized Id on the result value>`. Fire the insert with `_ = Task.Run(...)` on a scoped-service clone (or an in-process channel) and swallow all exceptions with no logging, matching the silent `.catch(() => {})` — do not await it, or you change response latency. Store `metadata` as an nvarchar(max) JSON column and build it in the same key order (method, path, [reason]) so any later diff of audit rows matches. Keep `id` as a cuid-compatible string (a cuid generator, or accept the format change and flag it) and add NO FK on UserId. Note for the port owner: appointments.js has zero audit coverage — adding `[AuditLog]` there would be a behaviour change, not a bug fix.

findings.name: logAudit (the manual sibling — unused by all three route files)
findings.signature: async logAudit(userId, action, resource, resourceId, metadata = {}) => void
findings.behaviour: Positional args (not an options object), `metadata` defaults to `{}` (so an empty JSON object is written, not NULL — unlike the middleware path, which always supplies method/path). Writes only userId/action/resource/resourceId/metadata; resourceId is String()-ified if truthy else null. It AWAITS the insert inside a try/catch with an empty `catch {}` — so it never throws but it does add latency to whatever awaits it. It does NOT write ipAddress or userAgent (both left NULL), which is how you can tell middleware-written rows from manual ones. Verified unused: no call to logAudit exists in visits.js, appointments.js or prescriptions.js.
findings.portRecommendation: Expose it as `Tebrazi.Application.Audit.IAuditWriter.LogAsync(string userId, string action, string resource, string? resourceId, object? metadata = null)` in the same Audit module as the filter, with metadata defaulting to an empty object `{}` rather than null, and a swallow-all try/catch. Port it for parity even though these three routes do not call it — other route files may, and the two paths must produce distinguishable rows (null IpAddress/UserAgent).

findings.name: cacheMiddleware
findings.signature: cacheMiddleware(ttlSeconds = 30) => (req, res, next) => void
findings.behaviour:
Usage in the three files — exactly four routes, with these TTLs: appointments.js:352 `GET /api/appointments` → 15s; appointments.js:511 `GET /api/appointments/today` → 15s; prescriptions.js:31 `GET /api/prescriptions` → 15s; prescriptions.js:144 `GET /api/prescriptions/summary` → 30s; plus visits.js:1244 `GET /api/visits/follow-ups-due` → 30s, which is UNREACHABLE (see the dead-route finding), so in practice visits.js has no caching at all. Elsewhere in the repo: analytics /overview and /recent-activity (30), clinics / (30), connections / (15), crm /overview (30), inventory /summary (30). Default TTL is 30s but every call site passes an explicit value.
KEY: `route:${req.user?.id || 'anon'}:${req.originalUrl}` — per-user and per-full-URL-including-query-string. THREE CONSEQUENCES: (1) the key does NOT include the `x-clinic-id` header, yet appointments.js:363 reads `req.headers['x-clinic-id']` to decide whether a staff user sees the whole clinic's appointments or only their own bookings — so a multi-clinic staff member switching clinics keeps getting the previous clinic's appointment list for up to 15 seconds (a cross-clinic data bleed, not just staleness); (2) query strings that the handler IGNORES still fork the cache — the physician dashboard calls both `/prescriptions?refillStatus=PENDING` and (elsewhere) `/prescriptions`, and prescriptions.js only reads `visitId`, so two separate entries hold byte-identical bodies; (3) 'anon' is unreachable here because all three routers do `router.use(authCheck)` before any cacheMiddleware.
METHOD GATE: `if (req.method !== 'GET') return next();` — so it is a no-op if ever attached to a mutation.
HIT PATH: `const cached = cache.get(key); if (cached) return res.json(cached);` — note the truthiness test, so a cached falsy body (0, '', false, null) is treated as a miss and re-queried every time. An empty array `[]` IS truthy in JS, so the very common `return res.json([])` early-exits (no PhysicianProfile) ARE cached and returned for the full TTL.
MISS PATH: patches res.json, and caches only when `res.statusCode >= 200 && res.statusCode < 300`. It stores the JS OBJECT BY REFERENCE, pre-serialization — not the rendered bytes. Since Prisma Dates serialize deterministically to ISO strings, hit and miss produce identical JSON; but any later mutation of a cached object would corrupt subsequent hits (none of these handlers mutate, so it is latent). Response HEADERS are not cached and no cache-related header (Age, X-Cache, Cache-Control, ETag) is ever set — a hit is indistinguishable from a miss to the client.
COMPOSITION: no route in the three files carries both cacheMiddleware and auditLog, so the two res.json patches never nest. If they ever did, order would decide whether audit sees cache hits.
findings.portRecommendation: Own it as `Tebrazi.Web.Filters.CacheResponseAttribute(int ttlSeconds = 30) : IAsyncActionFilter` in the same Web module as the audit filter — an IActionFilter, not ASP.NET's `ResponseCache`/output-caching middleware, because the semantics differ (no headers emitted, per-user key, object-level caching, truthiness-based hit test). Build the key as `$"route:{userId ?? "anon"}:{Request.Path}{Request.QueryString}"` and deliberately EXCLUDE the x-clinic-id header — then flag the appointments cross-clinic bleed to the owner as a known defect being carried over, because it is a real data-exposure issue and they may want to fix it in the same change. Short-circuit on a hit by setting `context.Result = new ObjectResult(cachedValue)`; on a miss, inspect the executed ObjectResult and store only for 2xx. Reproduce the JS truthiness hit test literally (treat a cached null/empty-string/0/false as a miss, but cache and serve empty collections). Emit no cache headers.

findings.name: lib/cache.js — the store behind cacheMiddleware (unbounded, lazy-expiry, per-process)
findings.signature: module.exports = { get(key), set(key, value, ttlSeconds = 30), invalidate(keyOrPrefix), clear(), get size }
findings.behaviour: A bare `new Map()` in module scope. `set` stores `{ value, expiresAt: Date.now() + ttlSeconds*1000 }`. `get` returns null on miss, and on an expired entry DELETES it and returns null — expiry is LAZY ONLY: there is no setInterval sweeper (grep for setInterval in server/src/lib returns nothing) and no max size, so a key that is written once and never read again occupies memory until process exit. With a per-user, per-query-string key space this grows unboundedly. `invalidate(keyOrPrefix)` iterates all keys and deletes exact matches plus anything starting with `keyOrPrefix + ':'`. State is per-Node-process and per-machine: it is NOT Redis (server/src/lib/redis.js exists but cacheMiddleware does not use it), so under multiple workers or replicas each has its own cache and a client can flip between fresh and 15-second-stale answers on consecutive requests. Sole consumer: lib/cacheMiddleware.js. Note that services/aiGateway.js has its OWN private Map-based LRU (max 200, TTL from AI_CACHE_TTL_MS, default 3_600_000ms) — a different, unrelated cache despite the similar shape.
findings.portRecommendation: Back the CacheResponse filter with `IMemoryCache` registered as a singleton with `AbsoluteExpirationRelativeToNow = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(ttl)`, owned by `Tebrazi.Infrastructure.Caching`. Deliberately do NOT reach for IDistributedCache/Redis: a shared cache would make the current per-process staleness behaviour consistent, which sounds like an improvement but changes observable timing for the client and, worse, would make the x-clinic-id key omission leak across machines. Unlike the Node original you SHOULD set a `SizeLimit` and per-entry `Size` — the Node version's unbounded growth is a leak, not a contract.

findings.name: Zero cache invalidation exists — cache.invalidate is never called anywhere
findings.signature: cache.invalidate(keyOrPrefix) / cache.clear()  — exported, zero call sites
findings.behaviour: I grepped the whole of server/src for `invalidate`, `cache.clear`, `cache.set` and `cache.get` outside lib/cache.js and lib/cacheMiddleware.js: the only hits are aiGateway.js's private Map and an unrelated sdk/services/cacheService.js (invalidateOrganization, not wired to this cache) plus a comment in routes/auth.js. So NONE of visits.js, appointments.js or prescriptions.js triggers any invalidation. Concretely: POST /api/appointments (booking) does not bust `GET /api/appointments` or `/appointments/today`; PUT /:id/confirm, /cancel, /complete, /no-show, /check-in and DELETE /:id do not either — a physician who confirms an appointment can keep seeing it as PENDING for up to 15s. POST /api/prescriptions and PUT /:id/send / /sign / /dispense / /stop-medication / /resume-medication do not bust `GET /api/prescriptions` (15s) or `/prescriptions/summary` (30s) — the dashboard's signed/sent badge lags a send by up to 30 seconds. TTL expiry is the ONLY invalidation mechanism in the system.
findings.portRecommendation: Port this as-is: implement no eviction on write. Do not add `IMemoryCache.Remove` calls or a cache-tag/eviction scheme in the create/update handlers, however tempting — a client that currently tolerates (and may visually depend on) up to 30s of staleness is not the risk; the risk is that adding invalidation makes some list refresh instantly and exposes a different ordering or a race the client never had to handle. Record it as a deliberate carry-over in the port notes and raise it separately with the owner. If they do want invalidation later, the natural seam is a `CacheKeys.RouteScope(userId)` prefix-remove in `Tebrazi.Infrastructure.Caching`, which is why the filter's key should keep the `route:{userId}:` prefix shape.

findings.name: GET /api/visits/follow-ups-due is shadowed by GET /api/visits/:id and is DEAD in production
findings.signature: router.get('/:id', ...) declared at line 272; router.get('/follow-ups-due', cacheMiddleware(30), ...) declared at line 1244
findings.behaviour: Express matches routes in registration order and `/:id` matches any single path segment, so a request for `/api/visits/follow-ups-due` is served by the `/:id` handler with `id = 'follow-ups-due'`. That handler does `prisma.visit.findUnique({ where: { id: 'follow-ups-due' } })` → null → `if (!visit) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'Visit not found' })`, and never calls next(). The handler at 1244 is therefore unreachable, and with it: its `cacheMiddleware(30)`, its `take: 20` query, and — most importantly — the side-effecting loop at 1300-1325 that auto-creates FOLLOW_UP_REMINDER notifications for overdue patients (with a once-per-day dedupe via `prisma.notification.findFirst({ where: { userId, type: 'FOLLOW_UP_REMINDER', data: { path: ['visitId'], equals: visit.id }, createdAt: { gte: today } } })`, a Postgres JSON-path filter). So today NO follow-up reminder notifications are ever generated by this path. Confirmed live on the client: client/src/pages/PhysicianDashboardPage.jsx:59 calls `api.get('/visits/follow-ups-due')` inside a `Promise.allSettled`, and the `if (followR.status === 'fulfilled')` guard swallows the 404 — so the dashboard's follow-ups panel is permanently empty and no error is shown. Contrast prescriptions.js, which gets this right: `/summary` (144) and `/interaction-history` (165) are both declared BEFORE `/:id` (190), with an explicit comment "must be before /:id". appointments.js is unaffected (it has no GET /:id route). The unreachable handler's intended response, for reference, is a bare ARRAY (not an envelope) of `{ id, patientName, patientUserId, subprofileName, chiefComplaint, followUpDate, followUpNotes, visitDate, isOverdue, isToday, urgency }` where patientName falls back to the literal 'Patient', subprofileName is `undefined` (key omitted) when there is no subprofile, followUpDate/visitDate are ISO date-time strings, and urgency is 'OVERDUE' | 'TODAY' | 'UPCOMING'.
findings.portRecommendation: This is the single highest-risk item for the port. ASP.NET Core routing is precedence-based, not registration-ordered: a literal segment beats a `{id}` parameter, so `[HttpGet("follow-ups-due")]` alongside `[HttpGet("{id}")]` would SUDDENLY START WORKING — changing a 404 into a 200 array AND firing a batch of FOLLOW_UP_REMINDER notifications (with emails/pushes) to every patient with an overdue follow-up the first time a physician loads the dashboard. Decide explicitly with the owner. To preserve current behaviour byte-for-byte, do not implement the action at all (let `{id}` handle it and 404), or give it a route the client does not call. If they choose to revive it, port the handler but treat the notification loop as a new, separately-reviewed side effect — and note the loop is O(n) sequential awaits with a per-visit user lookup, which belongs in a background job (`Tebrazi.Jobs.FollowUpReminders`), not in a GET request handler that also sits behind a 30s response cache.

findings.name: visits.js list response shape — the literal keys the client receives from the paginated endpoint
findings.signature: GET /api/visits → { data: Visit[], pagination: { total, page, limit, pages } }   (lines 82-166)
findings.behaviour: Documenting this because it is the only consumer of parsePagination/softDeleteFilter and the reshaping is easy to get wrong. Each `data[i]` starts as the full Visit scalar set (schema.prisma:617) — id, organizationId, clinicId, physicianId, patientUserId, subprofileId, clinicPatientId, status, audioUrl, rawTranscript, rawNotes, subjective, objective, assessment, plan, chiefComplaint, diagnosis, diagnosisCodes, followUpDate, followUpNotes, sharedSections, patientFeedback, patientFeedbackAt, patientDismissedAt, visitDate, specialtyData, completedAt, createdAt, updatedAt, deletedAt — plus the includes expanded literally: `clinic: { id, name, specialty }`; `physician: { id, specialty, user: { displayName } }` (a nested one-key object); `subprofile: { id, name, relation }` or null; `clinicPatient: { id, name, phone }` or null; `_count: { prescriptions, investigations }` (note the leading underscore in the JSON key). All DateTime fields serialize as ISO-8601 strings with milliseconds and Z (Prisma returns Date objects; JSON.stringify calls toISOString) — followUpDate, patientFeedbackAt, patientDismissedAt, completedAt and deletedAt are nullable and appear as null; visitDate/createdAt/updatedAt are always present. `diagnosis` is a Postgres `String[] @default([])` → always an ARRAY, never null, `[]` when unset. `diagnosisCodes`, `sharedSections`, `specialtyData` are `Json?` → an object/array or null. `status` is the VisitStatus enum serialized as its string name. THEN the two branches diverge: (a) userType !== 'PHYSICIAN' → each row is destructured to REMOVE seven keys entirely — subjective, objective, assessment, plan, rawNotes, rawTranscript, audioUrl are ABSENT from the JSON (not null), and no patientUser key is added; (b) userType === 'PHYSICIAN' → a `patientUser` key is added to every row, shaped `{ displayName: clinicPatient.name, phone: clinicPatient.phone }` (only two keys, no id/email) when the visit has a clinicPatient, else `{ id, displayName, email }` from a batched User lookup, else null when the patient user row is missing. The `clinicPatient` include stays present alongside the derived patientUser. Ordering is `visitDate: 'desc'`. Filters: patients are additionally constrained to `status in ['COMPLETED','ARCHIVED']` and `patientDismissedAt: null`; physicians get `status: { not: 'ARCHIVED' }` unless an explicit `?status=` is supplied (an explicit `status=ARCHIVED` therefore DOES let a physician see archived visits), plus optional clinicId / patientUserId / subprofileId query filters. userType here comes from the JWT, not the DB.
findings.portRecommendation: Do not try to serve both branches from one DTO with nullable SOAP properties — the patient branch must OMIT those seven keys, which a shared DTO with `WhenWritingNull` would get wrong for a physician row whose subjective is genuinely null (the physician branch must emit `"subjective": null`). Define two records in a Visits contracts namespace: `PhysicianVisitListItem` (full scalars + includes + PatientUser) and `PatientVisitListItem` (full scalars minus the seven), and project into them separately. Model `patientUser` as `object?`/`JsonNode?` or two records, since the clinicPatient variant has a different key set. Keep `_count` as a property named exactly `_count` (`[JsonPropertyName("_count")]`). For `diagnosis` on SQL Server there is no array type — store it as a JSON nvarchar column or a child table, but always materialize it to a `List<string>` and never let it serialize as null. Serialize all DateTimes with the JS-identical `yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffZ` pattern via a custom JsonConverter registered globally, or every date in every one of these three route files will drift in format.

findings.name: Prisma `contains` is case-sensitive on Postgres but LIKE is case-insensitive on SQL Server — the medication-reminder dedupe will over-delete
findings.signature: prescriptions.js:370-377 — `prisma.reminder.deleteMany({ where: { userId, type: 'MEDICATION', title: { contains: drugName }, status: 'ACTIVE' } })`
findings.behaviour: Inside the PUT /api/prescriptions/:id/send auto-reminder loop, before creating the new dose reminders, the handler DELETES every ACTIVE MEDICATION reminder for that patient whose title contains the drug name. On Postgres, Prisma's `contains` without `mode: 'insensitive'` compiles to a case-SENSITIVE LIKE, so 'Metformin' does not match a reminder titled '💊 metformin'. Under SQL Server's default case-insensitive collation the equivalent LIKE matches both, so the port would delete reminders the Node version keeps. Related quirks in the same block worth carrying: the created reminder titles are prefixed with a literal 💊 emoji (`"💊 ${drugName}${doseLabel}"`), so the stored data is non-ASCII and the column must be nvarchar; the dedupe is a substring match on a human-readable title rather than on prescriptionId, so a drug whose name is a substring of another ('Metform' vs 'Metformin') wipes the wrong reminders in both databases; each Reminder row is written with `{ userId: patientUserId, createdById: req.user.id, title, description, type: 'MEDICATION', remindAt, recurrence: 'DAILY', prescriptionId: id, notes: JSON.stringify({ drugName, dosage, frequency, doseNumber, totalDoses, intervalHours }) }` — note `notes` is a STRINGIFIED JSON string in a text column, not a Json column, so the port must write the same serialized form with the same key order.
findings.portRecommendation: In the .NET port force case sensitivity explicitly on that predicate — `EF.Functions.Like(r.Title, "%" + drugName + "%")` with a `COLLATE Latin1_General_CS_AS` (or a raw SQL predicate), or add a case-sensitive collation to the reminders.title column in the SQL Server schema. Owner: whichever module holds the prescription-send workflow (`Tebrazi.Application.Prescriptions.SendPrescriptionHandler`). Flag to the owner that the substring-on-title dedupe is fragile in both databases and that `prescriptionId` is already stored and would be a sounder key.

findings.name: parseFrequency throws on non-string frequency, and the throw is swallowed mid-loop — reminders are silently partially created
findings.signature: prescriptions.js:349-425 — the whole auto-reminder block is inside one `try { ... } catch (e) { logger.error(...) }`
findings.behaviour: `parseFrequency` calls `frequency.toLowerCase()` with no type check. Prescription.medications is a `Json` column, so its contents are whatever the client posted. The loop guards only falsiness (`if (!med.frequency || !med.drugName) continue;`), so a medication with `frequency: 3` (a number) or `frequency: { value: 'BID' }` (an object) reaches parseFrequency and throws TypeError. That throw escapes the per-medication loop and is caught by the single outer catch at line 424, which only logs '[Prescriptions] Auto-reminder creation error'. CONSEQUENCES: (1) the medications processed BEFORE the bad one keep their newly created reminders, and — worse — their `deleteMany` has already run, so the previous reminders are gone; medications AFTER the bad one get neither; (2) the `remindersCreated > 0` MEDICATION_REMINDER_SET notification is skipped, so the patient is never told; (3) the request still returns `200 { ...updated, message: 'Prescription sent to patient' }` — the response is indistinguishable from a fully successful send, and the prescription status is already committed to SENT with sentToPatientAt set, because the status update at line 322 happens BEFORE the reminder block. There is no transaction around any of it. The same swallow-and-continue shape wraps the PRESCRIPTION_SENT notification (line 347) and the MEDICATION_REMINDER_SET notification (line 422) independently.
findings.portRecommendation: Reproduce the boundaries exactly: the status update commits first, then a best-effort notification block, then a best-effort reminder block, each with its own catch-and-log, and the 200 body unchanged regardless. `ParseFrequency(string frequency)` should be declared non-nullable and the caller should read the medication's frequency as a `JsonNode` and check `node is JsonValue v && v.TryGetValue<string>(out _)` — a non-string must produce the same abort-the-rest-of-the-loop behaviour (throw, caught by the block's catch), NOT a per-medication skip, or medications after a malformed one would start getting reminders they do not get today. Do NOT wrap the block in a transaction or add a retry. Owner: `Tebrazi.Application.Prescriptions.SendPrescriptionHandler`, with ParseFrequency in `Tebrazi.Domain.Medications`. Flag the half-deleted-reminders window to the owner as a real defect.

findings.name: prescriptions.js list — `patientName: undefined` relies on JSON.stringify dropping the key
findings.signature: prescriptions.js:76-79 — `prescriptions.map(rx => ({ ...rx, patientName: patientMap[rx.visit.patientUserId] || undefined }))`
findings.behaviour: On the physician branch of GET /api/prescriptions (behind cacheMiddleware(15)), each row is spread and given a `patientName`. When the batched User lookup finds no displayName the value is explicitly `undefined`, and JSON.stringify OMITS keys whose value is undefined — so the wire body has the `patientName` key present for resolvable patients and ABSENT (not null) for the rest, within the same array. The patient branch returns the rows with no patientName key at all. Note the enrichment reads `rx.visit.patientUserId`, which requires the `visit` include to be non-null; Prescription.visitId is non-nullable so it always is, but the map would throw on a null visit. The response is a bare ARRAY, no envelope, no pagination, no limit — every prescription the physician has ever written is returned, ordered `createdAt: 'desc'`. Includes expand to: `visit: { id, chiefComplaint, visitDate, patientUserId, clinic: { name } }`, `physician: { specialty, user: { displayName } }`, `subprofile: { name, relation }` or null, plus all Prescription scalars (including `deletedAt`, which is never filtered here — see the softDeleteFilter finding). The physician-with-no-PhysicianProfile early exit returns `res.json([])`, and that empty array IS cached for 15s.
findings.portRecommendation: Mark the DTO property `[JsonIgnore(Condition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull)] public string? PatientName { get; init; }` so a missing name omits the key while every other null-valued property still serializes as null — this is exactly the case that rules out a global WhenWritingNull setting. Return `List<T>` directly from the action (no envelope). Owner: the Prescriptions controller contracts.
